images.filename: Coastal headland on the Cardigan Bay - geograph.org.uk - 705408.jpg
images.caption: Coastal headland on the Cardigan Bay. Rough grassland interspersed with gorse is the dominant vegetation here.  The hills along the coast form a watershed.  As a consequence there are only short streams running off directly to the sea, sometimes ending in waterfalls and always dug deeply into the hillside.  The east side of the coastal ridge drains towards the Ystwyth and Wyre rivers which have created sizeable breaches in the cliffs around their estuaries at Aberystwyth 222251 and Llanrhystud 359030.
images.alt: Coastal headland on the Cardigan Bay. Rough grassland interspersed with gorse is the dominant vegetation here.  The hills along the coast form a watershed.  As a consequence there are only short streams running off directly to the sea, sometimes ending in waterfalls and always dug deeply into the hillside.  The east side of the coastal ridge drains towards the Ystwyth and Wyre rivers which have created sizeable breaches in the cliffs around their estuaries at Aberystwyth 222251 and Llanrhystud 359030.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

images.caption: Cardigan Bay from 30,000 feet. On a flight from Luton to Kerry the plane crossed the Welsh coast at Cardigan.  The town can be seen in the bottom right of the photo with the Afon Teifi wending its way to the sea.  Cardigan Island can be seen just to the right of centre.  Although this image covers 20 or more squares I have allocated it to the Poppit Sands square which is just below the centre of the picture.  For next aerial image see 773942
